description: Ecological systems, energy flow, nutrient cycles, and ecosystem services

entries.ecosystem_definition: A biological community of interacting organisms together with their physical environment

ecosystem_components.abiotic: Non-living: temperature, precipitation, sunlight, soil, water, minerals

energy_flow.primary_production: Conversion of solar energy to chemical energy by producers
energy_flow.ten_percent_rule: Only ~10% of energy transfers between trophic levels; rest lost as heat
energy_flow.ecological_pyramid: Energy decreases at each level; mass usually follows same pattern
energy_flow.food_web: Complex network of feeding relationships; more stable than simple food chains

nitrogen_cycle.process: N₂ in atmosphere → fixed by bacteria → amino acids → proteins → decomposed → N₂O and N₂
nitrogen_cycle.fixation: Rhizobium bacteria in legume root nodules fix atmospheric N₂
nitrogen_cycle.importance: Nitrogen is limiting factor for most plant growth

nutrient_cycles.phosphorus_cycle: No atmospheric reservoir; weathered from rock; moves through soil, water, organisms

tropical_rainforest.location: Near equator; Amazon, Congo, SE Asia
tropical_rainforest.characteristics: High biodiversity; 50% of all species; 250+ cm rain/year
tropical_rainforest.threats: Deforestation; 17% of Amazon lost in last 50 years

coral_reef.characteristics: Most biodiverse marine ecosystem; 25% of ocean species; 0.1% of ocean area

grassland.importance: Most productive agricultural land; wheat, corn, soy
grassland.threats: Conversion to cropland (70% of grasslands converted)

wetlands.importance: Water filtration, flood control, carbon storage, habitat

ecosystem_services.regulating: Climate regulation, flood control, water purification, pollination
ecosystem_services.supporting: Nutrient cycling, soil formation, primary production
ecosystem_services.economic_value: Nature's services estimated at $125 trillion/year (more than global GDP)

ecological_relationships.mutualism: Both species benefit (+/+); e.g., bees and flowers
ecological_relationships.commensalism: One benefits, other unaffected (+/0); e.g., barnacles on whale
ecological_relationships.parasitism: Parasite benefits, host harmed (+/-); e.g., tapeworm
ecological_relationships.predation: Predator benefits, prey dies (+/-); regulates population sizes
